findings.title: T-2 cannot be done with the files and functions it names
quotes: `src/nio/cli.py`, `tests/test_explain.py`
Wire `check explainer` and the `explain` group into the CLI (CT-10)
Binding: `src/nio/explain.py:check` (new)
Assert: exit 1; `ERROR explainer missing: .nio/specs/checkout-refunds/explainer.md`.
- Test: TC-5, TC-6, TC-11, TC-12, TC-13, TC-16, TC-39
findings.fix: put `src/nio/explain.py` in T-2's Files and say which stubs it creates, or move the `check explainer` wiring to T-3 and the `explain` group to the tasks that build `finish` and `topic`. Give T-2 a test that passes when T-2 is done.

sources.situation: T-2 is the only task that wires `check explainer` (CT-10 dispatches it to `explain.check`, which is a new function in `src/nio/explain.py`). T-2's Files list has only `cli.py` and `test_explain.py`, so a worker following it has no `explain.check` to dispatch to. The `explain` group also dispatches `finish` (built by T-5) and `topic` (built by T-13), which do not exist at T-2. T-2's only test, TC-16, expects `ERROR explainer missing: ...`, and that message comes from the plan-mode checks that T-3 adds. Two outcomes: the worker edits `explain.py` outside its file list to write stubs, or TC-16 fails and T-2 is never done.

findings.reason: T-2 Files omit `src/nio/explain.py`, yet CT-10 dispatches to `explain.check` (new), `finish` and `topic`; its only test TC-16 asserts `ERROR explainer missing`, which T-3 builds (T-3 also lists TC-16). Nothing in tasks.md settles it.
findings.note: T-2 lists explain.py with check/finish/topic stubs; TC-16 passes at T-2

findings.title: T-1's only test needs a later task, and two of its three functions have no test
quotes: ### T-1 Add `sections`, `nodes` and `render` (CT-1, CT-2, CT-3)
exit 1 and the output holds `ERROR too many nodes: Calls (21 > 20)`
`explain.nodes` of the `Calls` block returns 21 IDs
findings.fix: give T-1 unit-level tests for `sections`, `nodes` and `render` (with the fake `npx`), and move TC-5's check assertions to T-3.

sources.situation: a worker finishes T-1 with `nodes` correct, so `explain.nodes` on the 21-ID chain returns 21. TC-5 also asserts `nio check explainer` exits 1 with `ERROR too many nodes`, and that check is built in T-3, so TC-5 cannot pass at T-1. Nothing in T-1 tests `sections` (CT-1) at all, and `render` (CT-3) is first tested by TC-14 and TC-15 in T-4. The worker has no passing test that proves `sections` or `render` works, and the one test it has needs a later task.

findings.reason: TC-5 (tests.md) also runs `nio check explainer` and asserts `ERROR too many nodes`, which needs the T-3 check (T-3 lists TC-5 too); T-1 lists only TC-5, so `sections` and `render` have no test until TC-6 (T-3) and TC-14/15 (T-4).
findings.note: Accept as risk: build as planned; the helpers are exercised by the next tasks' tests, and the epic jury checks every test passes before the epic closes.

findings.title: T-13's tests never call `explain.topic`
quotes: ### T-13 Add `explain.topic` and the topic-mode check (CT-6, CT-4)
- Test: TC-25, TC-42
an empty name → `error: the topic "<text>" gives an empty file name`
Assert: `auth-tokens-explainer-2.md` exists holding `(topic: auth/tokens)`
findings.fix: give T-13 a unit test of `topic()` covering the `//` refusal, the `Auth / Tokens!` slug, the same-text `continue:` and a clash that gives `-2`. Leave the e2e versions in T-14.

sources.situation: TC-25 runs the check on a topic path, and TC-42 runs `flow next`, `check` and `status` on a plan-named topic file. Neither calls `explain.topic`. The slug rule, the `continue:` or `new:` choice, the `-2` clash and the empty-name refusal are first asserted by TC-23 and TC-27, which are e2e tests in T-14 and need a real model under `NIO_E2E=1`. A worker can finish T-13 with `topic` wrong and see it only when T-14 runs on a model.

findings.reason: tasks-executability: T-13 now cites TC-23, TC-26 and TC-27, which are e2e tests that need a real model under NIO_E2E=1. No unit test of `topic()` covering the `//` refusal, the slug, the `continue:` case or the `-2` clash was added, so T-13 still cannot be shown done without a model run.
findings.note: Accept as risk: the real-model tests cover topic naming and run when the epic closes; a slug bug costs a paid model run to find.

findings.title: T-7's only test checks finish, not the gate it changes
quotes: ### T-7 Make the plan gate ignore the quickstart `Read first` line (CT-9)
- Test: TC-4
`artefact` reads every gate's files through `planned`, not only the tasks gate's
the third has no `back` line and `state: tasking`; `--approved` exits 0
findings.fix: add to T-7's Test a gate check: `planned` strips the line, and `nio check plan --approved` stays exit 0 after finish has added it (the third state of TC-30).

sources.situation: T-7 is done when TC-4 passes. TC-4 only checks that finish writes the line once, and it never runs the gate. The gate ignoring the line is first tested by TC-30's third state in T-12. Consider the real case: finish adds the line after the plan gate has passed, so a `planned` that doesn't strip it changes quickstart.md's bytes and the plan gate reopens. A worker whose `jury.artefact` or `flow.scan` still reads the line raw passes TC-4 and reports T-7 done.

findings.reason: TC-4 (tests.md) runs `nio explain finish` twice and checks the line appears once; it never runs the gate, and its Covers list is CT-5 and CT-10, not CT-9. The gate behaviour (`--approved` exit 0 with the line) is only in TC-30, assigned to T-12.
findings.note: T-7 cites TC-30, the gate check

findings.title: T-5 is tested only by its refusal, and rated effort low
quotes: ### T-5 Add `explain.finish`: refusals, hashes, drill-down markers, one atomic write (CT-5 steps 1-4, 7, 8)
- Test: TC-43
writes one source line per spec.md, plan.md and contracts.md
Tier: strong: refusals, hashes and an atomic write, specified by the contract
findings.fix: name in T-5's Test each step's test (TC-43 for step 2, and TC-8 or a unit test for step 1, TC-47 for step 3, TC-44 for step 4, TC-4 for step 8), or split T-5. Rate effort med.

sources.situation: T-5 has eight ordered steps: plan refusal, drill-down refusal, the drill-down marker, the hash and diagrams rules with the still-stale line, the images and drill-down lines, and the atomic write with the quickstart line. Its only test is TC-43, which checks the drill-down refusal alone. A worker can skip the marker or the still-stale line and still have T-5 pass. Those steps are only tested by TC-47 and TC-44 in T-11, and the quickstart line by TC-4 in T-7. Effort low undersells eight ordered steps with an atomic write, so the worker has no signal to test them in T-5.

findings.reason: T-5 lists only TC-43, the drill-down refusal. The marker (TC-47) and the still-stale line (TC-44) are assigned to T-11, and the quickstart line (TC-4) to T-7. Steps 1, 3 and 4 of T-5 have no test in T-5; the effort-low rating is a lesser side point.
findings.note: Accept as risk: build as planned; the helpers are exercised by the next tasks' tests, and the epic jury checks every test passes before the epic closes.
